Project Python Foundations: FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Marks: 60

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

  • The total order time (food preparation + delivery time) is significantly higher on weekdays compared to weekends, wehre the total time is shortened.

    • There could be an opportunity for incentives/rewards for ordering on the weekends if FoodHub wants to increase those numbers, considering that is when our customers typically are using the app.
      • OR a chance to increase weekday rewards by offering incentives for days that fall within a weekday to increase or distribute our numbers throughout the entire week.

Question 13: The company wants to provide a promotional offer in the advertisement of the restaurants. The condition to get the offer is that the restaurants must have a rating count of more than 50 and the average rating should be greater than 4. Find the restaurants fulfilling the criteria to get the promotional offer. [3 marks]¶

In [426]:
# Process used to calculate rated restaurants (excluding "Not given"), then converting to interger. From there, group the restaurants and necessary information (count and mean), and then calculate all information combined to show restaurant names, counts > 50 and mean > 4
df_rated_restaurants = df[df['rating'] != 'Not given'].copy()
df_rated_restaurants['rating']= df_rated_restaurants ['rating'].astype(int)
restaurant_ratings = df_rated_restaurants.groupby('restaurant_name')['rating'].agg(['count', 'mean'])
promotional_restaurants = restaurant_ratings[(restaurant_ratings['count']>50) & (restaurant_ratings['mean']>4)]
print('Restaurants that fulfill the criteria for the promotinal offer are:')
print(promotional_restaurants)

Question 14: The company charges the restaurant 25% on the orders having cost greater than 20 dollars and 15% on the orders having cost greater than 5 dollars. Find the net revenue generated by the company across all orders. [3 marks]¶

In [427]:
def rev(x):
  if x > 20:
    return x * 0.25
  elif x > 5:
    return x * 0.15
  else:
    return x * 0
df['revenue'] = df['cost_of_the_order'].apply(rev)

Question 15: The company wants to analyze the total time required to deliver the food. What percentage of orders take more than 60 minutes to get delivered from the time the order is placed? (The food has to be prepared and then delivered.) [2 marks]¶

In [430]:
# First determine total order time, then determine how many of those are over 60 minutes total. From there, calculate the number of orders over 60, and divide by the total number of orders in the dataset to uncover the percentage.
df[total_order_time] = df['delivery_time'] + df['food_preparation_time']
orders_over_60_minutes = df[df['total_order_time']>60]
num_orders_over_60_minutes = len(orders_over_60_minutes)
total_orders= len(df)
percentage_of_orders_over_60 = (num_orders_over_60_minutes/total_orders)*100
print (f"Number of orders over 60 minutes: {num_orders_over_60_minutes}")
print(f"Number of total orders: {total_orders}")
print(f"Percentage of orders that take more than 60 minutes to get delivered is: {percentage_of_orders_over_60:.2f}%")

Number of orders over 60 minutes: 200
Number of total orders: 1898
Percentage of orders that take more than 60 minutes to get delivered is: 10.54%

Observations:¶

  • The percentage indicates to us the rate of how often customers are experiencing total order times exceeding that of 60 minutes (1 hr). A higher percentage of orders exceeding 60 minutes could lead to higher customer dissatisfaction.

  • This metric could help FoodHub identify areas of improvement to reduce delivery times or pinpoint reasons for orders meeting &/or exceeding this threshold.

Question 16: The company wants to analyze the delivery time of the orders on weekdays and weekends. How does the mean delivery time vary during weekdays and weekends? [2 marks]¶

In [431]:
# calculate the average delivery times for both weekend and weekdays
mean_delivery_time_weekend = df[df['day_of_the_week']== "Weekend"]['delivery_time'].mean()
mean_delivery_time_weekday = df[df['day_of_the_week']== "Weekday"]['delivery_time'].mean()
print(f"The average delivery time for weekday deliveries is: {mean_delivery_time_weekday:.0f} minutes")
print(f"The average delivery time for weekend deliveries is: {mean_delivery_time_weekend:.0f} minutes")

The average delivery time for weekday deliveries is: 28 minutes
The average delivery time for weekend deliveries is: 22 minutes

Observations:¶

  • There is a distinct difference in mean delivery times, with weekend deliveries being significantly faster (around 22 minutes) compared to weekday deliveries (around 28 minutes).
  • This should be further investigated, but could be caused by the following:
    • Higher Driver Availability: More delivery personnel might be working on weekends to meet anticipated higher demand, leading to better allocation and quicker pick-ups/drop-offs.
    • Less Traffic Congestion: While centered in New York, weekend traffic patterns might be less congested than New York's regular weekday rush hours, allowing for faster travel times.
  • Implications for Weekday Deliveries: The longer weekday delivery times could indicate:
    • Fewer Available Drivers: Insufficient delivery personnel during weekdays might stretch delivery times.
    • Increased Road Congestion: Commute traffic during weekdays can naturally slow down delivery speeds.
    • Restaurant Capacity: Restaurants might face more dine-in or other order types during weekdays, potentially impacting the efficiency of FoodHub orders.

Recommendations:¶

Enhancing Customr Experience & Engagement:

  • Improve Customer Ratings Engagement -
    • It could be a good idea to introduce post-delivery reminders (“Rate your meal and earn 5 reward points”).
    • Provide micro-incentives such as $5 off next order for rating that have been provided in 10 minutes.
    • Add a one-tap rating option to reduce friction and commitment to time spent in the rating experience.

Optimizing Restaurant Operations & Delivery Based on Prep Times:

  • Suggest participating restaurants pre-prep popular items during peak hours.
  • Encourage popular restaurants to use FoodHub's “estimated prep-time feedback” to optimize staffing and improve overall customer experience/satisfaction.
  • Highlight fast-prep cuisines (cuisines) in the UI with labels like “Quick Bites” to maximize picks and emphasize these picks at peak production portions of the day (i.e., lunc time).

Stregthen High - Value Customer Retention:

  • Possibly implement a loyalty tier program (i.e., free delivery after every 5 orders).
  • Provide personalized offers to some of our top customers, like discounts on their most-ordered cuisine.
  • Encourage referrals (loyal customers → new customers).

Manage Weekday vs. Weekend Demand:

  • It could be a good idea to increase delivery partner availability on the weekdays to maintain fast delivery times.

  • Run weekday-only promotions to spread the upcoming demand (i.e., “$3 Off Thursday”).

  • Business Model & Revenue Strategy:

Increase Profit form High - Value Orders:

  • Create premium upsell prompts (“Add dessert +$6”).

  • Promote bundled meals for customers already spending above $20.
